questions.question: What defines fixed windows?
What two parameters define sliding windows?
A ten-minute window slides every five minutes. How many windows contain an event at 10:07?
What causes a session window to end?
options: An inactivity gap longer than the session threshold

questions.question: Why can a late event change existing session structure?
options: It can bridge two sessions that previously appeared separate
Late events always start a global window
It changes the event key automatically

questions.question: Why is joining fixed windows directly to session windows conceptually risky?
options: Their temporal groups may have no unambiguous one-to-one relationship
All Beam joins require global windows

questions.question: What does a watermark estimate?
What does allowed lateness control?
options: How long window state accepts late updates after on-time progress

questions.question: Why can one stalled source partition delay results?
options: The combined watermark may be limited by its slowest input
All partitions share one ordering key

questions.question: What is a cost of increasing allowed lateness?
options: It retains more state and correction responsibility
It makes every event on time
It reduces the number of active keys

questions.question: Allowed lateness is one hour. An event arrives after the watermark is two hours past its window end. What should happen?
options: It follows the configured too-late path, such as drop, quarantine, or correction
It moves to the current window

questions.question: Most events arrive within ten minutes, but rare financial corrections arrive days later. What is often preferable?
options: Use a bounded streaming lateness plus a reconciliation path

questions.question: What does a trigger decide?
options: When a window emits a pane
Which object store holds source files
Whether a message has a schema

questions.question: What does accumulating mode emit?
options: Only events since the prior pane
The full updated aggregate so far

questions.question: Accumulating panes emit 80, 100, and 103. What final total should an upsert sink hold?
What does discarding mode emit after each firing?
options: Only contributions since the previous firing

questions.question: Why should pane keys avoid worker attempt IDs?
options: Attempt IDs change on retry and can create duplicate logical panes

questions.question: Why is per-element triggering often operationally poor?
options: It can overwhelm sinks and checkpointing with excessive updates

questions.question: What does at-least-once delivery permit?
options: Exactly one external side effect automatically

questions.question: What produces effectively-once output?
options: At-least-once execution with deterministic identity and idempotent writes

questions.question: Why can an external HTTP call run twice despite exactly-once runner state?
options: The call may not participate in the runner's checkpoint transaction

questions.question: What is a limitation of time-bounded event-ID deduplication?
options: A duplicate arriving after expiry can be processed again

questions.question: Why is incrementing a counter directly unsafe under at-least-once delivery?
options: A redelivery can increment the same logical contribution twice
All increments are transactional across systems

questions.question: Which statement is a testable processing guarantee?
options: Every valid event affects the keyed daily total once if received within seven days

questions.topic: Pub/Sub Delivery Semantics: Acks, Ordering Keys, Dead-Letter Queues
questions.question: When should a subscriber acknowledge a message?
options: After its required durable effect is committed
Only after the topic is empty

questions.topic: Pub/Sub Delivery Semantics: Acks, Ordering Keys, Dead-Letter Queues
questions.question: What scope do ordering keys normally provide?
options: One total order for every topic
Ordering within a key under documented conditions

questions.topic: Pub/Sub Delivery Semantics: Acks, Ordering Keys, Dead-Letter Queues
questions.question: Why should one global ordering key be avoided?
options: It serializes traffic and destroys parallelism

questions.topic: Pub/Sub Delivery Semantics: Acks, Ordering Keys, Dead-Letter Queues
questions.question: What is the purpose of a dead-letter queue?
options: Isolate repeatedly failing messages for investigation and replay

questions.topic: Pub/Sub Delivery Semantics: Acks, Ordering Keys, Dead-Letter Queues
questions.question: Why should replay retain the original stable event identity?
options: It preserves deduplication and prevents duplicate effects

questions.topic: Pub/Sub Delivery Semantics: Acks, Ordering Keys, Dead-Letter Queues
questions.question: A poison message blocks later events for one ordering key. What is the sound recovery policy?
options: Retry forever and block the key
Use bounded retries, dead-letter it with context, then repair and replay
Acknowledge every later message first regardless of semantics
